item.research_question: Can machine learning models predict the phases of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with high accuracy?
key_findings: XGBoost and Random Forest models achieved 97% accuracy in predicting solid solution phases
XGBoost model achieved 86% accuracy in predicting all 11 phase categories
The inclusion of IM phases had a more pronounced impact on accuracy compared to the inclusion of AM phases
Mixing enthalpy and VEC are important features for predicting phase stability in HEAs
Atomic radius is a effective descriptor for distinguishing between BCC and AM phases
item.mechanism: The authors propose that the machine learning models can learn the complex relationships between the features and the phases of HEAs, allowing for accurate predictions
item.limitations: The dataset is imbalanced, with some phase categories having more records than others
item.future_work: The authors suggest that future work should focus on exploring the use of other machine learning models and features to improve the accuracy of phase predictions
quotes: XGBoost and Random Forest consistently outperform the other models, achieving 86% accuracy in predicting all phases
The inclusion of IM phases had a more pronounced impact on accuracy compared to the inclusion of AM phases

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can machine learning models predict the phases of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with high accuracy?. System: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) with 50 different elements. Findings: XGBoost and Random Forest models achieved 97% accuracy in predicting solid solution phases; XGBoost model achieved 86% accuracy in predicting all 11 phase categories; The inclusion of IM phases had a more pronounced impact on accuracy compared to the inclusion of AM phases; Mixing enthalpy and VEC are important features for predicting phase stability in HEAs; Atomic radius is a effective descriptor for distinguishing between BCC and AM phases. Mechanism: The authors propose that the machine learning models can learn the complex relationships between the features and the phases of HEAs, allowing for accurate predictions. Limitations: The dataset is imbalanced, with some phase categories having more records than others. Future work: The authors suggest that future work should focus on exploring the use of other machine learning models and features to improve the accuracy of phase predictions. Quote: "XGBoost and Random Forest consistently outperform the other models, achieving 86% accuracy in predicting all phases"

item.material_system: High-Entropy Alloys (HEAs) with varying compositions, including FCC, BCC, BCC+FCC, IM, BCC+IM, FCC+IM, BCC+IM, BCC+FCC+IM, AM, BCC+AM, FCC+AM, and BCC+FCC+AM phases
key_findings: 1. The BCC structure is the most frequently mentioned in the literature, closely followed by the FCC structure.
2. The dual-phase structure combining both FCC and BCC is also commonly discussed.
3. The majority (93%) of the data falls within the range of four to six components.
4. The alloys in the dataset consist of 50 different elements.
5. Certain elements, including Fe, Ni, Cr, Co, Al, Cu, Ti, Mn, V, Zr, Mo, Nb, Ta, and Zn, are more commonly used in the fabrication of HEAs.
6. The Adaptive Synthetic Sampling approach was used to generate synthetic data and mitigate class imbalance issues.
7. The ExtraTreesClassifier algorithm was employed for feature selection, resulting in 12 features suitable for HEAs phase classification.
quotes: The dataset utilized in this paper was sourced from various references,,,, encompassing 11 different categories and comprising a total of 11,252 records of HEAs.
The BCC structure is the most frequently mentioned in the literature, closely followed by the FCC structure.
The cleaned dataset, as summarized in Table 1, provides valuable insights into the frequency of occurrence for each phase category.
